title: Student Identification via Submission Data
description: The student ID included in the assignment submission could be used to identify the student to unauthorized parties, potentially enabling profiling or tracking across systems.
assumptions: Student ID is transmitted in clear or accessible format

title: Student Account Usurpation
description: Weak authentication mechanisms could allow an attacker to impersonate a student and submit assignments on their behalf, compromising academic integrity and privacy.
assumptions: Authentication system has vulnerabilities

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Submission Data
description: Work files, student IDs, and course information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, inadequate access controls, or data breaches.
assumptions: System has security vulnerabilities or insufficient access controls

title: Linkability of Student Data Across Systems
description: Submission data could be linked with other student records (grades, personal information, other courses) to create comprehensive profiles, potentially violating privacy expectations.
assumptions: Data is stored in interconnected systems without proper anonymization

title: Excessive Data Collection
description: The system may collect more data than necessary for the grading process, including work files that could contain sensitive personal information beyond what's needed for academic assessment.
assumptions: Data retention policies are not aligned with minimization principles

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student and Course Information
description: Student IDs, course information, and file references transmitted from the Grades Portal Web App could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission, potentially exposing sensitive academic data.

title: Data Manipulation of Submission and Grading Requests
description: Assignment and grading request data could be altered in transit between the portal and the Assignment & Grading Service, potentially modifying grades, file references, or student/course information.

title: Identification of Students via Academic Data
description: Student IDs and course information transmitted in the data flow could be used to identify specific students, potentially enabling tracking of academic activities and performance.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grading Service Data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service could be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems, exposing student IDs, course information, file references, and requesting role data.

title: Data Manipulation within Grading Service
description: Data stored or processed within the Assignment & Grading Service could be tampered with by malicious actors, potentially altering grades, assignment records, or student information.

title: Usurpation of Requesting Role
description: An attacker could impersonate a legitimate requesting role (e.g., instructor, administrator) to access or modify grading data, potentially leading to unauthorized grade changes or data access.

title: Student Identifiability from Assignment Data
description: The assignment store contains student ID, course, and submission time, which can be used to identify specific students and their academic activities.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Assignment Files
description: Assignment files and associated student metadata could be accessed by unauthorized parties if the datastore lacks proper access controls and encryption.

title: Linkability of Student Records
description: Student ID enables linking this assignment data to other student records, creating a comprehensive profile of student activities across systems.

title: Assignment Submission Usurpation
description: Unauthorized individuals could potentially submit assignments on behalf of students, compromising academic integrity and data authenticity.

title: Unauthorized Access to Submission Queue
description: Teacher account could be compromised, allowing unauthorized individuals to access the submission queue and view student work.
assumptions: Weak authentication or credential theft

title: Excessive Disclosure of Student Submissions
description: Teacher may access student submissions beyond what is necessary for grading, potentially exposing sensitive student information.
assumptions: Teacher has broad access permissions without granular controls

title: Linkability of Teacher Identity to Submission Review Patterns
description: Teacher's access patterns to submission queues could be linked to their identity, revealing teaching behavior and preferences.
assumptions: Access logs are retained and analyzed

title: Data Minimization Violation in Submission Display
description: Grades Portal may display more student data than necessary for the teacher's grading task, including potentially sensitive information.
assumptions: System displays full submission content rather than summarized grades

title: Identification of Teacher Through Access Patterns
description: Teacher could be identified through their unique access patterns to submission queues, potentially revealing their teaching assignments.
assumptions: Access logs are publicly accessible or improperly secured

title: Student Identifiability Through Direct Name Disclosure
description: Student names are directly included in the data flow, making individual students identifiable to the teacher and potentially to others with access to the portal.
assumptions: Teacher has legitimate access to view student submissions

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student Work Content
description: Student work content and submission times could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the portal's access controls are compromised or if the teacher's credentials are stolen.
assumptions: Portal has proper authentication and authorization mechanisms

title: Linkability of Student Submissions Across Time
description: Submission times combined with student names and work content could be used to link multiple submissions to specific students, creating detailed behavioral profiles.
assumptions: Submission timestamps are recorded and accessible

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance with Student Data Protection Laws
description: Sharing student names, work content, and submission times may violate FERPA, GDPR, or other educational data protection regulations if proper consent and safeguards are not in place.
assumptions: Institution has data protection policies in place
uncertainty_note: Specific regulatory requirements vary by jurisdiction

title: Student and Grader Identification via IDs
description: The data flow includes student ID and grader ID fields that can directly identify individuals. If these IDs are not properly anonymized or if they can be linked to other data sources, students and teachers could be identified from the grades portal.
assumptions: IDs are not pseudonymized and can be cross-referenced with other systems

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Grades and Feedback
description: Written feedback and grades may contain sensitive information about student performance that could be disclosed to unauthorized parties if access controls are inadequate. Feedback might include personal observations or comments that reveal more than intended.
assumptions: Access controls may not be properly enforced

title: Linkability of Student Performance Data
description: The combination of student ID, grader ID, grade, and feedback text could be used to link multiple data points to create a comprehensive profile of student performance and teacher evaluation patterns, potentially enabling tracking across different contexts.
assumptions: Data can be correlated across systems or time periods

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Grade Submission
description: Teachers may be able to deny submitting grades or feedback after the fact, which could lead to disputes and undermine the integrity of the grading process. Without proper audit trails, accountability is compromised.
assumptions: No immutable audit logging is in place

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: The grading service could be accessed by unauthorized individuals, leading to disclosure of sensitive student grade information including grades, feedback, and personal identifiers.

title: Student Identification from Grade Data
description: Student IDs combined with course and grade information could be used to identify specific students, potentially enabling tracking of academic performance across courses.

title: Linkability of Grade Records with Other Data
description: Grade records containing student IDs could be linked with other student data sources (e.g., enrollment records, personal information), creating comprehensive student profiles.

title: Data Breach of Grade Records Database
description: The Grade Records Database could be compromised through security vulnerabilities, leading to mass disclosure of student grades and feedback to unauthorized parties.

title: Unauthorized Modification of Grade Records
description: Attackers could potentially modify grade records in the database, leading to grade tampering, feedback manipulation, or grader ID forgery.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Student Grades
description: Student grades and feedback could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, data breaches, or improper sharing mechanisms in the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Assumes inadequate access controls or security vulnerabilities in the system

title: Identity Usurpation for Grade Access
description: An attacker could impersonate a student to access their grades and feedback through credential theft, session hijacking, or social engineering attacks.
assumptions: Assumes authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to credential compromise

title: Grade Data Integrity Compromise
description: Student grades and feedback could be tampered with, modified, or deleted by unauthorized actors, leading to inaccurate academic records.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient integrity controls or audit logging

title: Linkability of Grades to Student Identity
description: Grades could be linked to student identity in ways that create privacy risks, such as enabling profiling or tracking of academic performance patterns.
assumptions: Assumes grades are stored with identifiable information

title: Student Identification from Grade Data
description: Student identity could be inferred or directly identified from their grades and feedback data, potentially exposing sensitive personal information.
assumptions: Assumes grades contain or can be correlated with identifying information

title: Unauthorized Access to Student Grades
description: Grades and teacher feedback transmitted from the portal to the student could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission or storage.

title: Student Identity Impersonation
description: An attacker could impersonate a student to access their grades and teacher feedback through compromised credentials or session hijacking.

title: Linkability of Student Data
description: Grades and feedback could be linked to other student data or external identifiers, potentially revealing patterns about the student's academic performance or identity.

title: Excessive Data Disclosure to Student
description: The portal may display more detailed grades or feedback than necessary for the student's legitimate needs, potentially exposing sensitive academic information.

title: Unauthorized Account Access
description: Parent's login credentials could be compromised, allowing unauthorized individuals to access child's grades and personal information.
assumptions: Weak authentication or credential theft

title: Unauthorized Grade Disclosure
description: Child's grades could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through the web app, violating privacy expectations and potentially FERPA/GDPR compliance.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls or data leakage

title: Child Identification via Grades
description: Grades combined with other data could be used to directly identify the child, even if the child's name is not explicitly shown.
assumptions: Grades are unique enough to identify individuals

title: Parent-Child Identity Linking
description: Parent's identity could be linked to child's academic records, potentially revealing family relationships or enabling profiling across systems.
assumptions: Account linking creates traceable connections

title: Grade Data Inaccuracy
description: Grades displayed in the portal could be inaccurate, outdated, or corrupted, affecting the parent's ability to make informed decisions.
assumptions: Data entry or processing errors

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child's Academic Data
description: Child's grades, feedback, and submission history could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through insecure transmission or improper access controls in the Grades Portal Web App.

title: Linkability of Academic Data with Other Records
description: The child's academic data could be linked with other personal or educational records, creating a comprehensive profile that exceeds the intended scope of the data sharing.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grades Portal
description: Unauthorized individuals could access the Grades Portal Web App and view sensitive academic information about the child, including grades and submission history.

title: Improper Identification of Authorized Parent
description: The system may fail to properly verify the identity of the parent, allowing unauthorized individuals to access the child's academic data under the guise of being a parent.

title: Misrepresentation of Academic Performance
description: The parent could potentially misrepresent or falsify the child's grades, feedback, or submission history when using the data for external purposes.

title: Unauthorized Account Data Manipulation
description: Malicious actors could exploit weak authentication or access controls to modify student/parent account data (names, emails, roles, relationships) without authorization, leading to false records and potential identity fraud.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls, weak authentication mechanisms, or lack of audit logging

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Personal Information
description: Sensitive personal data (names, emails, parent-child relationships) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through improper access controls, data leaks, or insufficient encryption during storage/transmission.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls, lack of encryption, or improper data handling procedures

title: Unauthorized Identification of Individuals
description: Unauthorized parties could identify specific students or parents through account data (names, emails, relationships) if the system lacks proper anonymization or access restrictions.
assumptions: Insufficient access controls, lack of data minimization, or inadequate privacy-by-design measures

title: Administrator Impersonation
description: Attackers could impersonate the school administrator to create, modify, or disable accounts if authentication mechanisms are weak or compromised, leading to unauthorized account management.
assumptions: Weak authentication, lack of multi-factor authentication, or credential theft

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Account Actions
description: Without proper audit trails, administrators could deny performing account modifications (creation, modification, disabling), making it difficult to hold them accountable or investigate incidents.
assumptions: Missing or inadequate audit logging, lack of immutable logs

title: Data Integrity Compromise in Account Records
description: The Assignment & Grading Service writes account records to the Account Directory. If an attacker gains unauthorized access to modify these records, it could corrupt grading data, alter student information, or create false parent-child relationships, compromising the integrity of the entire system.
assumptions: Attacker has access to the data flow or the grading service

title: Unauthorized Modification of Parent-Child Relationship Links
description: The grading service writes parent-child relationship links to the Account Directory. An attacker could modify these links to create false familial relationships, potentially for identity fraud, privilege escalation, or social engineering attacks.
assumptions: Attacker can access or manipulate the data flow between P2 and DS3

title: Identification via Account Records
description: The Account Directory stores account records that may contain personally identifiable information (PII). If accessed by unauthorized parties, these records could be used to identify individuals, potentially leading to identity theft or stalking.
assumptions: Account records contain PII and are accessible to unauthorized parties

title: Linkability of Parent-Child Relationships
description: The parent-child relationship links stored in the Account Directory could be used to link different records together, potentially revealing family connections that individuals may wish to keep private. This could lead to unwanted profiling or social engineering.
assumptions: Parent-child relationships are stored in a way that allows linking across records

title: Data Disclosure of Sensitive Account Information
description: The Account Directory may contain sensitive account information (e.g., grades, personal details). If this data is disclosed to unauthorized parties, it could lead to privacy violations, discrimination, or other harms.
assumptions: Account records contain sensitive information and proper access controls are not enforced

title: User Unawareness of Data Writing
description: Users may not be aware that the Assignment & Grading Service is writing their account records and parent-child relationships to the Account Directory. This lack of awareness could lead to consent issues and privacy violations.
assumptions: Users are not informed about the data flow and its implications

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Student Data
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transmitted to an external cloud hosting provider, creating risk of unauthorized disclosure of sensitive personally identifiable information (PII) and educational records.

title: Data Integrity Compromise During Transmission
description: During nightly backup and replication transmission to the cloud provider, data could be tampered with, altered, or corrupted, compromising the integrity of grade records and assignment data.

title: Linkability of Student Records Across Systems
description: Account directory and grade records sent to the cloud provider could be linked with other data sources, enabling tracking of students across multiple systems and contexts.

title: Identification of Individuals from Backup Data
description: The account directory and grade records contain sufficient PII to identify individual students, creating identification risks when data is stored on external cloud infrastructure.

title: Unintended Use of Educational Data
description: Cloud hosting provider may use the transferred grade and assignment data for purposes beyond the intended backup/hosting function, such as profiling or commercial exploitation.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance with Data Protection Laws
description: Transferring full student records to external cloud provider may violate data protection regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) regarding cross-border data transfers and third-party data processing.

title: Unauthorized Access to Grade Records
description: Grade records database contains sensitive personal information about students, parents, and teachers. Unauthorized access could lead to privacy violations and potential misuse of educational data.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls on the grade records database

title: Inappropriate Data Exposure in Views
description: Assignment & Grading Service builds student, parent, and teacher views that may expose grade records to unauthorized parties or in contexts where they shouldn't be visible.
assumptions: View generation logic lacks proper access controls

title: Student and Parent Identification
description: Grade records can be used to identify specific students and their parents, potentially enabling doxxing or targeted harassment.
assumptions: Grade records contain identifiable information

title: Cross-Reference Linkability
description: Grade records could be linked with other data sources (e.g., student IDs, parent contact info) to create comprehensive profiles of individuals.
assumptions: Multiple data sources exist that can be correlated

title: Educational Data Privacy Compliance
description: Handling of grade records may violate educational privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) if proper consent and data protection measures are not implemented.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements exist for educational data
